title: Additional Drivers Declared on a Trip and the Young-Driver Surcharge Rate
content:
Percentage points go onto the young-driver surcharge rate on a Keyturn Trip Booking where additional drivers have been declared on the trip's protection election and the reserved period is a long one. The declaration is carried on the election made under the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan for that trip, and what is read is the number of additional drivers declared on it.

1. Where two or more additional drivers are declared on the trip's protection election and the reserved period runs for 14 days or more, the additional-driver adjustment is 4 percentage points on.
2. Where one additional driver is declared on the trip's protection election and the reserved period runs for 14 days or more, the additional-driver adjustment is 2 percentage points on.
3. In every other case no additional-driver adjustment is made, which is to say the adjustment is 0.

### The combinations

| Additional drivers declared on the protection election | Length of the reserved period | Additional-driver adjustment (percentage points) |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | 14 days or more | 4 |
| Exactly 1 | 14 days or more | 2 |
| None | 14 days or more | 0 |
| Any number | Fewer than 14 days | 0 |

The length of the reserved period runs from the first day of that period to the last, both days counted, and 14 days is reached rather than passed.

*Hypothetical.* A reserved period of 30 days whose protection election declares 3 additional drivers takes 4 percentage points. The same reserved period with 1 additional driver declared takes 2 percentage points, and with none declared takes 0. A reserved period of 9 days takes 0 however many additional drivers are declared on its protection election.
